# Frozen song layout and body selection

This scalar oracle separates two existing timing contracts. The original renderer rounds local times for each independently rendered song. Native format-1 schedules round shared absolute clock endpoints; a rack-local range subtracts the already-rounded origin. No clock, event format, acoustic fixture, or audio tolerance changes here.

The 72 original Focus plans come from the unchanged revision 9 `SessionPlanner`, seed 91031, with the accepted first song enabled. The verifier extracts and evaluates the actual `session_render.py` AST expressions for allocation length, body start/end, placement origin, and `mix[lo:hi]`. The manifest records those expressions and source hashes. Original timing is `N = round((duration + 5) * 32000)`, with the half-open body from beat 16 to the outgoing transition's start. The first accepted song has 3,711,911 logical frames and body `393846..<3150769`; the fresh meter therefore consumes 2,756,923 frames.

Local rounding is deliberately preserved even at nonzero song origins. Original songs 5, 7, and 10 distinguish it from subtracting rounded absolute endpoints. An additional expression-only duration of 123.000078125 seconds distinguishes the original five-second allocation expression (4,096,003 frames) from rounding the form first and adding 160,000 (4,096,002). That diagnostic changes the duration input to the original expression; it is not an independently generated musical plan.

Five native layouts reuse the plans in the unchanged `planning-v1` fixture: its three selected schedules and two fractional-origin variants. Their independent clock calculation uses the original ramp integral with absolute shared endpoints. Native length is the canonical form-end frame minus the canonical origin, plus exactly 160,000 tail frames. Body endpoints likewise subtract the rounded origin. The two variants construct the incoming transition at `96 + 0.25/32000` and `96 + 0.5/32000` seconds. Every integer layout field must match exactly, with zero frame tolerance. Native clocks are not retimed to match the original renderer's local rounding.

Four bounded stream recipes test selecting a body from supplied post-HP32 stereo Float32 samples. Intro and tail values are nonzero and excluded from the meter. One body is silent after a loud intro, detecting incorrectly inherited K-weighting history; another has 24,000 frames, preserving the original floating half-tie block count. A 64,000-frame level sequence exercises both gates. The musical case reuses the existing one-second original body excerpt without duplicating PCM. It is a body-selection diagnostic, not a full-song loudness result.

Recipe indices start at the body's first frame. Pattern samples are `Float((i % 31) - 15) / 64` on the left and `Float((i % 17) - 8) / 32` on the right. The level recipe applies the listed dyadic scale starting at each body-local index; the scale changes at the next listed start. All other samples equal the case's `outside` pair. These recipes can be generated into bounded buffers. The frozen expectation comes from the original AST crop followed by unchanged, freshly initialized pyloudnorm. Input/body SHA256s and absolute/relative gate memberships are retained. Measurable status and all counts are exact; finite LUFS error is limited to 0.00001 LU. Silence is represented as `measurable: false, lufs: 0` rather than serializing infinity.

`freeze-song-body.py` refuses replacement without explicit `--replace` and is never run by CI. `verify-song-body.py --integrity` checks source hashes, exact independently rederived layouts, strict metadata, recipes, and inventory without DSP dependencies. Default verification additionally reruns the original body measurements. `--compare` requires exactly `layouts.json` plus four case JSON files in an ignored `.build` directory. Layout candidates are an ordered array of flat records containing `id`, `origin_frame`, `input_frames`, `body_start_frame`, and `body_end_frame`. Each case result uses the existing six-field loudness schema. `--evidence` retains all exact layouts, scalar errors, and native file hashes.

These layouts count logical song frames. The five-second allocation tail is already included; glue's 399 physical startup/drain frames and peak protection's 160 frames do not enlarge the body or song range. The selector does not repair mixer origins, render a rack, apply gain, or enable playback. A complete analysis consumes the declared full logical stream while only its half-open body enters the fresh meter.
